machineCharacter.apx01: The reference formula car: huge downforce and brutal brakes, near neutral on the nose, and it spins if you floor it mid-corner.
machineCharacter.fx26: Electrified top-tier formula: more power and a quarter less downforce than the APX-01, so it launches harder and lifts earlier in fast sweeps.
machineCharacter.jf2: Feeder-series single-seater: two-thirds of the top cars' aero grip, firm brakes, and a rear that steps out when you floor it.
machineCharacter.fr3: Third-rung spec formula: honest balance, little speed lost weaving, and tow-heavy pack racing on modest power.
machineCharacter.fe4: First rung of the ladder: light, nearly neutral and planted under power, with a sharp turn-in on a lift and little power to cover mistakes.
machineCharacter.hf67: Sixties cigar-tube: light and quick in a straight line but short of grip on narrow tyres, so it pushes, then spins when you add power.
machineCharacter.hf76: Seventies winged formula: wide slicks and a big wing give real fast-corner grip and drag; a lift swings the tail round quickly.
machineCharacter.hf86: Turbo-era brute: huge power for its weight, and the boost arrives late, so it comes in a rush out of slow corners.
machineCharacter.vc62: Vintage club roadster: slow and soft with a long brake lead, forgiving until the tail swings out under power.
machineCharacter.hy9: Hybrid endurance prototype: low drag, a front motor that only joins in at speed, strong stable braking, and a rear that steps out on full throttle.
machineCharacter.hy11: Hybrid prototype with more downforce and less top speed than the HY-9, its torque helped by a small crankshaft motor.
machineCharacter.pr2: Closed spec prototype: near neutral and strong in fast corners, short of straight-line speed against the hypercars.
machineCharacter.pr3: Open-cockpit prototype: turbo torque and low-speed downforce, draggy on the straights and laggy at corner exit.
machineCharacter.sp71: Long-tail seventies prototype: very high top speed on little grip, so it pushes in corners and takes a long stop, but stays planted on power.
machineCharacter.gt8f: Front-mid V8 GT: stable under braking with torque out of slow corners; it pushes on turn-in and spins up on full throttle.
machineCharacter.gt10m: Mid-engine V10 GT: the most power of the four GTs, neutral-ish balance, and it spins less than the V8 under full throttle.
machineCharacter.gt6r: Rear-engine flat-six GT: the weight over the rear tyres gives traction and braking, staying planted on power while the light nose pushes.
machineCharacter.gt6s: Long front-engine straight-six GT: the stable, understeering heavyweight, with turbo torque that gets it up to speed quickly.
machineCharacter.gs4: Entry GT: easy-to-read turbo six with plenty of torque, the heaviest GT, and it lets go on full throttle at the limit.
machineCharacter.gs6m: Mid-engine entry GT: planted under power and neutral-ish, with about a quarter less torque than the GS-4 and a lighter nose.
machineCharacter.tc1: Front-drive touring saloon: stable on a lift and under braking, but it pushes wide as soon as you ask for power.
machineCharacter.tc2: Rear-drive touring saloon: rotates well on entry, then goes loose if you are early on the power.
machineCharacter.tc3: All-wheel-drive touring saloon: the best launch of the touring cars and planted on throttle, though it pushes on turn-in.
machineCharacter.cr1: Lightweight club roadster: low inertia and quick to rotate, with a tail that comes round fast on throttle or a lift; short of top speed.
machineCharacter.hh2: Front-drive hot-hatch racer: braking-stable and torquey, but the front tyres are overloaded on power and it pushes wide.
machineCharacter.rh3: Road hot hatch: usable torque and a soft front end that saturates on power out of slow corners.
machineCharacter.rl2: Rally car on gravel tyres: traction on any surface and short gearing, but very understeery and tall on asphalt.
machineCharacter.rl7: Seventies rear-drive rally saloon: light and tail-happy on throttle, very stable on a lift, short of grip and top speed.
machineCharacter.gb4: Group-supercar rally monster: violent acceleration and planted traction everywhere, understeering on asphalt.
machineCharacter.rcx6: Rallycross supercar: brutal sprint acceleration and abrupt power with short gearing; built for loose surface, very understeery on tarmac.
machineCharacter.rxe: Electric rallycross car: instant torque and no gear changes, but heavy and understeery in direction changes.
machineCharacter.dx8: Desert trophy truck: huge power in a heavy, tall body that rolls, brakes long and spins up on throttle; a loose-surface specialist.
machineCharacter.bg2: Desert buggy: lighter than the truck and quick to turn, but the tail swings on a lift and under power, and it brakes long.
machineCharacter.sk125: Shifter kart: enormous grip for its weight and very short stops for its speed, but a low top speed makes it slow on a big circuit.
machineCharacter.dk100: Direct-drive sprint kart: momentum and line discipline, slow off the line, with rear-only brakes that make it stop long.
machineCharacter.xf2: Fan-assisted prototype: grip and braking that do not wait for speed, the highest in the game, until a crest or kerb breaks the seal.
machineCharacter.xe1: Electric time-attack prototype: the quickest launch here and strong downforce in medium and fast corners, drag-capped on the straights.
machineCharacter.xh3: Hydrogen prototype: efficient low drag and four-wheel traction, but a single reduction gives up acceleration at the top.
machineCharacter.xt1: Track-only V12 hypercar: power everywhere, the highest top speed of any car, and a rear that spins up on full throttle.
machineCharacter.eh3: Electric road hypercar: instant torque and four-wheel traction launch it hard, but its mass pushes wide in every corner.
machineCharacter.sc7: Mid-engine road supercar: acceleration and top speed first, planted on power, with strong road-tyre braking.
machineCharacter.rs5: Four-door sports sedan: launch, torque and all-weather traction, with a heavy, understeery nose and mass in the braking zones.
machineCharacter.rm8: Front-engine muscle coupe: torque and a long top gear, planted under throttle until the tail snaps at the limit.
machineCharacter.rg63: Sixties grand tourer: a sweet high-revving V12 and a long top speed on narrow tyres, long to stop and rolling in corners.
machineCharacter.rp6: Performance pickup: goes anywhere with torque to spare, but mass and height give it the longest stop of any road machine.
machineCharacter.rr4: Rally-bred road car: traction on any surface, with turbo lag and understeer on power.
machineCharacter.lx12: Luxury grand tourer: effortless torque, top speed and great stability, the most understeery machine here and heavy in every corner.
machineCharacter.rd2: Light road roadster: balanced and easy to slide, a lift rotates it readily, short of power and top speed.
machineCharacter.gpr1: Prototype GP bike: wings, the highest top speed of any bike and the strongest lean grip; braking is stoppie-limited.
machineCharacter.gpr2: Second GP prototype: inline-four with more wing and drag, stops shorter but tops out and launches slower than the GP-R1.
machineCharacter.sbk1000: Production-based superbike: quick, but a step down from the prototypes in lean, braking and top speed, with kind electronics.
machineCharacter.ss600: Supersport: light and agile, revs hard to make its speed, with less power to correct a late line.
machineCharacter.nr900: Naked roadster: upright and draggy on road tyres, quick off the line, out of breath at high speed and long to stop.
machineCharacter.cr750: Seventies two-stroke racer: narrow tyres, the weakest brakes of any bike and a lean limit you can feel; delicate to ride.
machineCharacter.mx450: Four-stroke motocross bike: torque everywhere and a tall fifth for the straights; built for jumps, with long stops on asphalt.
machineCharacter.mx250: Two-stroke motocross bike: light and revvy, quicker off the line than the four-stroke but out of breath at the top end.
machineCharacter.sm450: Supermoto: the motocross chassis on road wheels, with the best tarmac grip and top speed of the dirt bikes, still long to stop.

wildcard: A formula car runs a mountain pass downhill in cold fog: stacked switchbacks, rock on one side and a long drop on the other.
Downforce cars on a 31-degree banked oval: three laps near 300 km/h with a safety wall at the mirrors.
Prototype hypercars race a harbour street circuit in a thunderstorm: a curving tunnel, 2.6 m walls and gusts off the water.
Shifter karts take a floodlit city circuit in the rain: two tunnels that stay dry, a riverside blast and a plaza corner.
Motocross bikes on a 31-degree banked tri-oval: knobbly tyres, safety walls and 110 km/h of pure nerve.
Prototype grand-prix bikes thread a docklands street circuit: concrete walls, a 9.9 m flyover and no bike-safe run-off.
Two-stroke motocross bikes on a tarmac circuit through a slot canyon, with rain due mid-race: 100 km/h dry, 70 wet.
Supermotos under the cranes of a floodlit container terminal, with rain due: a figure-eight with a flyover, built for cars.
Supermotos on a rallycross circuit in a dust storm: tarmac, rolled gravel and a crest jump; the joker road is for cars.
A full lap of a gravel rally stage in the rain on supermoto tyres: crests over the ridge, a hairpin and a watersplash.
One lap of a 20.8 km forest ring on a motocross bike: twelve minutes, 33 corners, blind crests and a banked hairpin.
Front-engine GT cars on a wet rallycross circuit: tarmac, mud, a crest and a hairpin they were never tuned for.
RALLYCROSS ON THE GRAND PRIX GRID
Rallycross cars on a full grand-prix circuit: built to slide, they now face two long tarmac straights.
Desert trucks on a floodlit city circuit: long-travel suspension, concrete walls and two tunnels.
DESERT TRUCKS ON THE ICED COL
Trophy trucks climb a mountain pass in a snowfall: loose snow on the climb, polished wheel tracks, 400 m of view in the squall.
Trophy trucks race a slot-canyon circuit inside a dust storm: 170 m of amber haze and a loose film over the tarmac, thinnest on the line.
Hot-hatch racers in a multi-storey car park: roofed ramps, pillar slaloms and two tight hairpins. It never rains inside.
Supermotos take a car park flat out: 4% ramps, pillar slaloms and a 1.4 km lap done in under a minute.
GRAND PRIX BIKES ON THE RUNWAY
Prototype grand-prix bikes on a salt-flat airbase: a two-kilometre runway, sweepers across the salt and a 230 km/h lap average.
A solo hot lap of a multi-storey car park in a hypercar with no ABS and no traction control, and walls 1.4 m off the asphalt.
ROAD MACHINES ON THE FOREST RING
A rally-bred road car, a muscle coupe, a supercar and a roadster take one lap of a 20.8 km forest ring as the light goes.
A supercar, a muscle coupe, a roadster and a rally-bred road car share a snowed-in resort road: six hairpins and a polished wheel track.
TROPHY TRUCKS ON THE SKI ROAD
Desert trucks take a ski-resort road in a snowfall: six hairpins, a ridge run and a roofed gallery where the snow stops.
Desert trucks race an airport at dawn in fog: a runway sprint, a blast-pad turn, taxiway chicanes and a slalom between the gates.
Prototype hypercars take an airport in a dust storm: a 1.6 km runway, taxiway chicanes and 170 m of amber haze on the apron slalom.
Shifter karts race a dam crest in a thunderstorm: concrete parapets, water 20 m below on both sides and gusts off the reservoir.
FORMULA CARS IN A GALE ON THE DAM
Formula cars cross a dam crest in a thunderstorm on wet tyres: a kilometre of concrete, 20 m of water either side and gusts off the lake.
Shifter karts race a night market in the rain: the covered halls stay dry, the open lanes do not.
Supermotos weave a night market: three hairpins, covered halls and a spice-row slalom, under the lamps.
loadingTips: Brake in a straight line, then release smoothly as you turn in.
Cold tyres have less grip. Build temperature on your first lap.
Harvest energy on the straights you do not need, deploy where you do.
Press C to change camera. The cockpit view gives the best sense of speed.
In the wet, avoid the painted kerbs and look for grip off the usual racing line.
Press P to request a pit stop and choose your next set of tyres.
A smooth exit is worth more than a late apex.
tips: A rallycross heat needs its joker laps: every one you are short costs a time penalty.
A smooth exit is worth more than a late apex.
Brake before the face of a jump, not on it.
Brake in a straight line, then release smoothly as you turn in.
Cold tyres have less grip. Build temperature on your first lap.
DRS opens inside a marked zone when you are within 1.0 s of the car ahead, in the dry, from lap 3. Press F; braking closes it.
Drive to an event marker, or travel to any discovered route from the world map.
Dry at the start; a storm arrives and later clears. Be ready to change tyres.
Dust storm: visibility drops to about 170 m and a loose film settles on the tarmac, thinner on the racing line.
Fog: visibility starts near 110 m and thins over about a quarter of an hour. The cold, damp surface costs a slick about a seventh of its grip.
Gold asks 40.96 s, silver 42.61 s, bronze 45.51 s or faster. The machine is loaned: nothing to buy.
Gold asks P1, silver P3, bronze P4 or better. The machine is loaned: nothing to buy.
Gold asks P1, silver P3, bronze P5 or better. The machine is loaned: nothing to buy.
Harvest energy on the straights you do not need, deploy where you do. E changes the hybrid mode.
Heavy rain leaves standing water: use full wets and stay off the painted kerbs.
In solo practice, land smoothly on each surveyed downslope to clear its target.
In the air, tap a brake to lower the nose, then release for touchdown.
Night sessions run under floodlights. Lighting is visual only and never changes grip or weather.
One lap decides it. A clean first corner is worth more than a brave last one.
Press C to change camera.
Press C to change camera. The cockpit view gives the best sense of speed.
Press P to request a pit stop and choose your next set of tyres.
Q / Z shift rider weight forward and back; release to settle.
Set your speed before turn-in, then ease the brake as lean builds.

Snow: the road starts covered. Deep snow grips about a quarter of dry; the worn, polished wheel tracks along the racing line about two-fifths. Stay in the tracks, brake early, and use full wets or a winter tread.
Storm: standing water about twice as deep as heavy rain, and gusts to 20 m/s push cars and bikes sideways. Give the wind room.
This event runs with no ABS and no traction control: the throttle and brake are yours alone.
Unwind lean, then add power gently.
Use the front brake for a strong stop; the rear pedal is a light touch.

changeable.brief: Dry at the start; a storm arrives and later clears.

rain.brief: Steady heavy rain from the start; standing water.

fog.brief: Cold dawn fog. Visibility starts near 110 m and thins over a quarter of an hour; the damp, cold surface costs a slick about a seventh of its grip and the tyres are slow to warm.

storm.brief: A 60 to 76 mm/h cell: standing water about twice as deep as heavy rain, gusts to 20 m/s that push cars and bikes sideways, a dark sky and lightning.

dust.brief: Hot desert dust storm: visibility drops to about 170 m, a strong gusting wind loads the bodywork, and a loose dust film settles on the tarmac, thinner on the racing line.

snow.card: Snowfall, packed snow and ice, sub-zero
snow.brief: Sub-zero snowfall on a snow-covered road: deep snow gives about a quarter of dry grip and the worn, polished wheel tracks along the racing line about two-fifths, so stay in the tracks. Visibility closes to 400 m in the squall. Winter tread helps.

auto.brief: The venue's own light: floodlit at the night venues, daylight everywhere else.

sunset.brief: A low sun and long shadows.

live.brief: The real sun, moon and stars over your location, on your clock.

circuit.label: CIRCUIT
circuit.skill: Braking points, tyre management and racecraft.

gp.label: GP BIKE
gp.skill: Lean angle, trail braking and the front/rear brake split.

dirt.label: DIRT
dirt.skill: Throttle on loose ground, jump take-off and landing, ruts and berms.

festival.label: FESTIVAL
festival.skill: Exploration, point-to-point, speed traps and drift zones.
